name: read_file
description:
Read content from one of your personal files.

Usage:
- Use this when you need to recall information: what you know about the other person, your current goals, or your relationships.
- The path must be relative to your personal directory. Examples: "knowledge/对方名.txt", "goals/current.txt", "relationships/某人.txt"
- Use line_start and line_count to read only what you need.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Relative file path within your character directory, e.g. "knowledge/对方名.txt"

parameters.name: line_start
parameters.description: Line number to start reading from (1-based). Omit to read from the beginning.

parameters.name: line_count
parameters.description: Number of lines to read. Omit to read to the end.

name: append_file
description:
Append new information to one of your personal files.

Usage:
- Use this when you learn something new about the other person: their identity, background, intentions, or opinions.
- Only write to files in your personal directory.
- Do NOT overwrite — new information is always appended, never replaced.
- The content should be a single concise sentence in Chinese.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Relative file path, e.g. "knowledge/对方名.txt"

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: A single sentence to append, in Chinese.

name: list_dir
description:
List files and directories within your personal directory.

Usage:
- Use this to discover what files you have (e.g., who you have relationship files for, what knowledge files exist).
- The path is relative to your character directory. Use "" for root.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Relative path to list, e.g. "" for root, "knowledge" for knowledge folder.

name: grep
description:
Search your personal files and world files for a keyword or phrase.

Usage:
- Use this before calling read_file — to find which files contain information you need and which lines to read.
- The pattern parameter is the keyword or phrase to search for (e.g., a person's name, a place, a topic, a date like 1084夏).
- The path parameter (optional) limits the search scope. Use "knowledge", "chat_logs", "relationships", "goals", "decisions", "World", or leave empty for all.
- max_results: maximum number of matches to return (default 20, max 100).
- context_lines: number of lines before/after each match to include (default 2), so you see the full entry, not just the matching line.
- case_sensitive: set true for case-sensitive search (default false).
- Returns each match as: file_path:line_number: (▶ marks the matching line) content, with surrounding context.
- This lets you pinpoint exactly which file and line to read, rather than guessing.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: The keyword or phrase to search for.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Subdirectory or file to limit search to. "knowledge", "chat_logs", "relationships", etc. "World" for world files. Empty or omitted for all of your directory.

parameters.name: max_results
parameters.description: Maximum number of matches to return. Default 20. Use a smaller number when you expect many matches.

parameters.name: context_lines
parameters.description: Lines of context before and after each match. Default 2. Use 0 for only the matching line.

parameters.name: case_sensitive
parameters.description: Whether the search is case-sensitive. Default false.

name: write_file
description:
Create a new file or overwrite an existing one entirely.

Usage:
- Use this to create a new record from scratch or replace all content in a file.
- The content replaces the entire file — use edit_file if you only need to change part of a file.
- Do NOT write to chat_logs/ or persona.txt.
- The path is relative to your personal directory.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Relative file path, e.g. "goals/current.txt"

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: Full content to write to the file.

name: write_chronicle
description:
Save a completed chronicle entry to the history archives (court historian only). The system names the file automatically as {名称}{体例}.txt in history/chronicles/, so the archives stay consistent.

Usage:
- Call this function whenever you have finished writing a chronicle entry and want to save it.
- The 体例 parameter must be exactly one of: 编年史 (annual record of the realm's events) / 本纪 (biography of a kingdom's ruler) / 世家 (the rise and fall of a kingdom or great house) / 列传 (biography of an individual) / 纪事 (monograph on a major event).
- The 名称 parameter is the subject name WITHOUT the 体例 suffix: e.g. 拉盖娅, 南帝国, 芬·格鲁芬多克, 1084, 帝国分裂.
- Do NOT include the 体例 word inside 名称 (pass 拉盖娅, not 拉盖娅本纪).

parameters.name: genre
parameters.description: 体例：编年史 / 本纪 / 世家 / 列传 / 纪事（四选一）

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: 史文主题名，不含体例字样，如 拉盖娅 / 南帝国 / 1084

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: 史文完整正文

name: glob
description:
Find files in your personal directory matching a pattern.

Usage:
- Use this to discover files by name pattern, e.g. "knowledge/*.txt" to list all knowledge files, or "goals/*" to find all goals.
- The pattern supports * (match anything) and ? (match one character).
- Returns matching file paths relative to your directory.
- The pattern is relative to your personal directory. Use "World/*.txt" for world files.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Glob pattern, e.g. "knowledge/*.txt", "relationships/*", "goals/new_*". Supports * and ? wildcards.

name: edit_file
description:
Perform exact string replacement in one of your personal files.

Usage:
- Use this to UPDATE outdated information — e.g., when query_character reveals someone's status has changed, replace the stale record with current facts.
- The old_string must match EXACTLY one occurrence in the file. Include enough surrounding context to make it unique.
- The old_string is replaced with new_string in-place.
- Do NOT edit chat_logs (conversation records are immutable) or persona.txt.
- The path is relative to your personal directory.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Relative file path, e.g. "knowledge/对方名.txt"

parameters.name: old_string
parameters.description: The exact text to find and replace. Must match exactly one occurrence.

parameters.name: new_string
parameters.description: The replacement text.

name: delete_file
description:
Delete one of your personal files.

Usage:
- Use this to remove obsolete records — completed goals, resolved decisions, outdated relationship notes.
- The path is relative to your personal directory.
- Do NOT delete chat_logs, persona.txt, or character.json.
- Deletion is permanent.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Relative file path to delete, e.g. "goals/old_plan.txt"

name: move_file
description:
Move or rename a file — useful for marking completed plans by moving them to a done/archive directory.

Usage:
- The old_path and new_path are both relative to your personal directory.
- Example: move_file("goals/plan_expand.txt", "goals/done_expand.txt")
- The target path must NOT already exist.
- This is equivalent to reading the file, writing it at the new path, then deleting the old.
- Do NOT move chat_logs, persona.txt, or character.json.

parameters.name: old_path
parameters.description: Current file path to move FROM.

parameters.name: new_path
parameters.description: New file path to move TO. Must not already exist.

name: send_letter
description:
Send a written letter to another entity. It is appended to your correspondence thread with the recipient (visible in the O panel) and they will be activated to respond — every letter costs real effort.

Usage:
- ONLY write when it is genuinely important: a vital notification, a necessary negotiation, an urgent warning, or a commitment that must be put in writing.
- Do not write casually or out of politeness. If silence is acceptable, stay silent — unnecessary letters waste the recipient's effort and yours.
- When you do write, make it count: clear, purposeful, complete in one letter.
- The content should be the full body of your letter, written in formal written style.

parameters.name: recipient_entity_id
parameters.description: The entity ID or Chinese name of the recipient. Use the [ID: xxx] shown in context if available, otherwise use the Chinese name (e.g. "拉盖娅").

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: The full body of the letter in Chinese.

name: submit_advisory
description:
Submit your public advisory to the king of your kingdom. The system will record it with a timestamp and archive it in the kingdom's public advisory records, visible to the court historian.

Usage:
- Call this when you have finished forming your advisory opinion and want to present it to the king PUBLICLY.
- The content should be the advisory text itself — no greeting, no signature, no meta commentary.
- The system automatically adds your name, title and the current time before your words.
- After calling this, reply with a brief closing line only; do not repeat the advisory in your reply text.
- If you have things you do NOT want written into history, use submit_secret_advisory instead.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: The body of your public advisory in Chinese. State your position directly (e.g. 支持/反对某事, 应当/不应如何).

name: submit_secret_advisory
description:
Submit a SECRET advisory to your king only. It is NOT recorded in the annals and the court historian cannot read it.

Usage:
- Call this when you think something should not be recorded in history or known by others — things only the king should hear.
- The king alone can read these; the historian and the public record will never see them.
- The content should be the advisory text itself — no greeting, no signature.
- After calling this, reply with a brief closing line only.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: The body of your secret advisory in Chinese, addressed only to the king.

name: submit_edict
description:
Publish a public edict to your whole kingdom — a royal decree, a policy statement, or a question posed to your vassals. The system will record it with a timestamp and archive it in the kingdom's edict records; your vassals read it before they advise, and the court historian may cite it in the annals. Only the ruler of the kingdom may issue edicts; anyone else is rejected by the system.

Usage:
- Call this when you have something to declare to the realm: a guiding policy, an answer to your vassals' advisories, or a question you want your vassals to address.
- The content should be the edict text itself — no greeting, no signature, no meta commentary.
- The system automatically adds your name, title and the current time before your words.
- After calling this, reply with a brief closing line only; do not repeat the edict in your reply text.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: The body of your edict in Chinese. Declare your will directly, or pose the question you want your vassals to answer.

name: consult_king
description:
Send an envoy to another kingdom's ruler to ask a question or verify information. The other ruler may answer, and their answer reaches you when you next review your kingdom's affairs. This inquiry is recorded as public diplomatic correspondence that the court historian may consult.

Usage:
- Call this when you want to ask another ruler something directly: to verify a rumor, sound out an intention, probe before an alliance or peace, or question a betrayal.
- Only the ruler of a kingdom may send envoys; anyone else is rejected.
- The target can be any kingdom, allied or enemy.
- There is a short cooldown between envoys to the same kingdom; if the envoy is still traveling you will be told.

parameters.name: target_kingdom
parameters.description: The name of the kingdom to ask (e.g. "北帝国" or "Battania").

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: The question or message to send to the other ruler, in Chinese.

name: reply_consult
description:
Reply to a diplomatic inquiry from another kingdom's ruler. Your answer is delivered back and recorded in the public diplomatic correspondence.

Usage:
- Call this when another ruler has sent you an envoy and you have decided what to answer.
- You may answer truthfully, mislead, or decline to say — the choice is yours.
- Only the ruler of a kingdom may reply; anyone else is rejected.

parameters.name: target_kingdom
parameters.description: The name of the kingdom whose ruler asked you.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Your answer to the other ruler, in Chinese.

name: send_envoy
description:
Send a secret envoy to another clan leader (a vassal, an independent lord, a mercenary captain, or a foreign king) to exchange private messages. Unlike letters, an envoy does not cascade — the recipient is woken once to answer, and the exchange stays private between you two.

Usage:
- Call this when you want to sound someone out, verify a rumor, propose a secret alliance, plot against your liege, or negotiate quietly.
- Only clan leaders can send envoys. You cannot send an envoy to yourself.
- target_entity_id is the recipient's entity ID or Chinese name.
- The content is the message your envoy delivers. Write it as a private message to the other person.
- The recipient will be woken to answer once; their answer reaches you the next time you review your own affairs. Do NOT send repeated envoys while awaiting a reply — the same envoy thread is used.
- There is a short cooldown before you can send another envoy to the same person.
- This correspondence is PRIVATE: the historian cannot read it, and no third party can read it. Only you and the recipient.
- Do NOT use this to send casual pleasantries; every envoy wakes the recipient once.

parameters.name: target_entity_id
parameters.description: The entity ID or Chinese name of the recipient clan leader (e.g. "博泰罗_CharacterObject_1664" or "拉盖娅").

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: The private message to deliver, in Chinese.

name: reply_envoy
description:
Reply to a secret envoy you received. Your answer is delivered to the sender and recorded in your private correspondence thread with them.

Usage:
- Call this when another clan leader has sent you a private envoy and you have decided what to answer.
- You may answer truthfully, mislead, decline to say, or propose a meeting — the choice is yours.
- The reply does not wake anyone again; the sender will see it the next time they review their own affairs.
- This correspondence is PRIVATE: the historian and third parties cannot read it.

parameters.name: target_entity_id
parameters.description: The entity ID or Chinese name of the clan leader who sent you the envoy.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Your answer to the sender, in Chinese.

name: record_resolve
description:
Record a resolve, decision, or note into your private diary (decisions/diary.txt) in the standard format. The system enforces the diary format so memory search stays reliable.

Usage:
- Call this when you reach a decision, make a commitment, form a plan or resolve, learn valuable intelligence, or change course during your self-review.
- The type must be one of: 决心 / 决定 / 承诺 / 计策 / 情报 / 评价 / 结果 / 战略.
- The content is a single concise sentence describing what you resolved or decided.
- The system adds the date prefix automatically; only append, never overwrite.
- Do NOT write '决心' items into diary via write_file/append_file — use this tool so the format stays valid.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Entry type: 决心 / 决定 / 承诺 / 计策 / 情报 / 评价 / 结果 / 战略.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: A single concise sentence in Chinese describing the resolve or decision.
